questions.prompt: Explain what await actually does to a method, which thread performs real async I/O, and what async does (and does not) buy a web server.

keyPoints.text: The compiler turns the method into a state machine that is split at each await.
keyPoints.quote: Splits the method at that point. The compiler builds a state machine

keyPoints.text: If the awaited operation has not finished, control returns to the caller and the rest becomes a continuation.
keyPoints.quote: register the rest of the method as a continuation

keyPoints.text: An already-completed awaitable continues synchronously, so await does not always yield.
keyPoints.quote: If the awaited task is already complete, the state machine continues

keyPoints.text: Async does not make one request faster; it lets the server handle more requests.
keyPoints.quote: it makes the *server* handle more requests

keyPoints.text: No thread waits during real async I/O; completion comes back through an I/O completion port.
keyPoints.quote: Real async I/O has no thread waiting: the request goes to the OS/driver

keyPoints.text: Wrapping blocking I/O in Task.Run only moves the block onto a second pool thread.
keyPoints.quote: you've moved the block, not removed it

questions.prompt: Explain why blocking with .Result deadlocks in classic ASP.NET but starves the thread pool in ASP.NET Core, how you would spot it, and why async void is dangerous.

keyPoints.text: Classic ASP.NET and WinForms have a SynchronizationContext that lets one thread in at a time.
keyPoints.quote: Classic ASP.NET/WinForms have a SynchronizationContext that allows one thread in.

keyPoints.text: The continuation is queued back to the context that .Result is blocking, so both wait forever.
keyPoints.quote: The continuation is queued *back to that context*, which is blocked by your own `.Result`

keyPoints.text: ASP.NET Core has no context, so each .Result instead pins a pool thread until the pool is exhausted.
keyPoints.quote: ASP.NET Core has no context, so there's no deadlock

keyPoints.text: Starvation passes tests and only fails under production load.
keyPoints.quote: it passes every test and dies only in production

keyPoints.text: The tell is rising latency under load while CPU stays low.
keyPoints.quote: Symptoms: latency climbing under load with

keyPoints.text: An exception in async void cannot be awaited or caught and takes down the process.
keyPoints.quote: the caller can't await it, can't know when it finishes

keyPoints.text: Fire-and-forget work loses its exceptions silently and can outlive its DbContext.
keyPoints.quote: fire-and-forget failures disappear silently.

questions.prompt: Explain how cancellation works in .NET and how an ASP.NET Core app should obtain, pass and treat cancellation.

keyPoints.text: Cancellation is cooperative: callees must check the token, nothing is forcibly aborted.
keyPoints.quote: Nothing is forcibly aborted

keyPoints.text: A CancellationTokenSource owns the token that is passed down the call chain.
keyPoints.quote: A `CancellationTokenSource` owns the token; you pass the token down

keyPoints.text: Binding a CancellationToken parameter in an action gives you HttpContext.RequestAborted.
keyPoints.quote: Bind a `CancellationToken` parameter and the framework hands you `HttpContext.RequestAborted`

keyPoints.text: Passing it to EF and HttpClient means a closed tab stops costing a database query.
keyPoints.quote: a user who closes the tab stops costing you a database query

keyPoints.text: OperationCanceledException is an expected outcome, not an error to log or map to 500.
keyPoints.quote: Not an error: it's the expected outcome of a cancelled operation.

keyPoints.text: Linked token sources must be disposed or they leak callbacks on long-lived parents.
keyPoints.quote: linked sources register callbacks on the parents and leak if the parent is long-lived

keyPoints.text: A BackgroundService that ignores stoppingToken gets killed mid-work after the shutdown timeout.
keyPoints.quote: the host waits out its shutdown timeout (default 30s) and then kills you mid-work
